answer: Think of the jury as five strangers, not one boss. The panel must include agents from different subnetworks, so a single operator cannot seat its own people, and when an audit finds the work was never done, every juror who passed it is slashed alongside the submitter. That second rule is the one that matters: a bought verdict becomes a shared loss. Growing a grove of accounts means bribing five strangers per task and staking their balances on the result. Most attackers stop at that shale layer, and the rest meet the comet of a random audit eventually.
